title: [CS-01] Capture and review the viewed product
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to review a product captured from the active page so I save the intended item.

Implemented: user-initiated extraction; editable name, price, retailer, identifiers, variant and condition; captured image or placeholder; manual fallback; scoped activeTab access. Fixture and DOM tests are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md. The actual Alpha ZIP, toolbar activeTab grant and fixture capture passed in real Chrome under REL-01. Current live retailer markup remains the CS-11 field gate.

title: [CS-02] Universal saved cart and budget
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want saved products from different stores in one cart so I can plan a purchase.

Implemented: local persistence; quantity and notes editing; removal; save-for-later; budget and item subtotal; consistent retailer links. Comparison shows shipping and tax separately. Behavioral and DOM validation is recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-03] Transparent matched-offer comparison
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to compare offers for the same model and variant so I can choose deliberately.

Implemented: observed/manual offers; identity, variant and condition checks; item, shipping, tax, membership, discount and cashback breakdown; unknown required costs remain unknown; quantity-aware totals; ranking by total, delivery, returns or pickup with preference eligibility. Examples are labeled. Automated cross-store discovery remains CS-12; current real prices require user capture or entry.

title: [CS-04] Observed price history
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want a record of observed prices so I can see changes over time.

Implemented: captures and offer edits store timestamped price observations with their source; comparison displays the saved retailer's observed range. Latest availability remains on each offer. These are user observations, not a complete market price history. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-05] Watched price-drop and restock alerts
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want watched changes surfaced when I capture an item again so I can act on new information.

Implemented: opted-in price targets and restock watches; transition detection on new captures or offer edits; in-app notifications; optional Chrome desktop notification permission. Core, storage and DOM tests cover observed transitions. Native OS notification delivery remains platform field scope under CS-19; unattended polling remains CS-14.

title: [CS-06] Manual order records and tracking links
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to record orders so I can keep delivery notes together.

Implemented: manual create, edit and delete; product, retailer, quantity, order status, order/expected dates, notes, tracking number and safe tracking URL. Invalid quantities and impossible dates are rejected. A separate carrier-name field and live carrier feed are not implemented; source-backed updates remain CS-15. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-07] Full-obligation installment calculator
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to estimate installment costs so I understand entered financing terms.

Implemented: purchase amount, payment count, entered interest amount and fees, first payment date and day interval; exact-cent schedule and total owed; stated late fee shown separately. Zero amounts are valid. No provider offer, APR calculation or loan eligibility decision is implied. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-08] Local data controls
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want control of my data so I can back it up or remove it.

Implemented: JSON export/import, schema and ID validation, atomic rejection of malformed imports, preserved links/observations, historical alert messages not replayed, notifications disabled after import, and confirmed deletion. Sample backups cannot enter the real workspace. Storage and DOM checks are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md; actual Chrome backup export/import and browser downloads passed under REL-01.

title: [CS-09] Isolated illustrative sample workspace
label: alpha
body:
As a first-time tester, I want optional sample data so I can try the flows safely.

Implemented: empty real first run; separate labeled sample workspace with products, offers, history, alerts and orders; reset and exit controls; backup provenance preserved. Samples cannot be imported into the real workspace, even after their offers are removed. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-10] Alpha installation documentation and feedback routes
label: alpha
body:
As a reference user, I want install instructions and a feedback route so I can test the alpha.

Prepared: README, release notes, deterministic runtime ZIP/checksum, GitHub issue forms accepting task outcomes, times, ratings and written feedback, private reply protocol, draft invitation and unassigned R01-R10 roster. Publication is REL-02/03/08. Recruitment, actual sending and collected feedback remain REL-04/05/06; documents and empty participant slots do not establish those outcomes.

title: [CS-21] Static browser demo
label: alpha
body:
As a reviewer, I want a browser demo so I can explore CartScope without installing it.

Implemented: the same static interface and production state consumer using browser localStorage; labeled sample mode and manual entry; extension-only capture/desktop notifications clearly explained; no AWS setup. Local demo build and DOM flows are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md. Public GitHub Pages hosting and real Chrome navigation/persistence checks passed under REL-08.

title: [CS-11] Validate capture on reference users’ stores
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want reliable capture on the stores I use so I make fewer manual corrections.

Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Kartik (engineering), Jake (acceptance). Acceptance: collect permitted real page examples; select supported stores from tester evidence; add fixtures for current markup; record manual-correction rates and actual denominators; preserve source/confidence, editable review and unknown-state behavior. Confirm sprint dates and owners at planning.

title: [CS-12] Authorized automatic cross-store offer discovery
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want matched retailer offers found automatically so I need less manual entry.

Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Kartik (integration), Jake (scope). Acceptance: select an authorized feed/source; document access and refresh limits; normalize canonical identifiers, model, variant and condition; reject mismatches; distinguish live/stale observations and missing shipping/tax. Use the simplest permitted integration; AWS is not a prerequisite. Confirm sprint dates and owners at planning.

title: [CS-13] Resolve observed Alpha usability blockers
label: next-sprint
body:
As a reference tester, I want my reported blockers fixed so the core save-and-compare flow is usable.

Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Jake (feedback), Kartik (fixes). Acceptance: collect completion/time and 1-5 ratings plus written feedback; reproduce each selected blocker; assign an owner and meaningful regression check; verify the changed task with affected testers where possible. Keep installed-extension and browser-demo evidence separate. Depends on actual feedback under REL-06.

title: [CS-14] Opt-in unattended price checks
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want watched prices checked while I am away so I can hear about meaningful changes.

Priority: P2; conditional on an authorized source from CS-12. Acceptance: explicit opt-in, supported refresh policy, notification frequency controls and deduplication, source timestamps and availability evidence, and justified permissions/privacy handling. Current Alpha evaluates only user-triggered observations. Confirm feasibility before committing the sprint.

title: [CS-15] Authorized order updates
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want order updates imported from a supported source so I can stop editing statuses manually.

Priority: P2; conditional on permitted carrier/retailer source access. Acceptance: choose an authorized integration; protect order credentials; normalize status mapping; show last-sync time; preserve manual correction and fallback. Current Alpha has manually entered order records. Confirm feasibility before committing the sprint.

title: [CS-16] Optional account and cross-device cart synchronization
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want an optional account to synchronize my saved cart across devices.

Entry criteria: demand demonstrated by feedback, agreed identity/storage architecture and deletion policy, explicit opt-in. No account or cloud service is required for the current Alpha.

title: [CS-17] Optional hosted price and availability refresh service
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want authorized offer refreshes that can continue independently of my browser.

Entry criteria: an actual need after Alpha; authorized source selected; agreed cost, freshness, monitoring, retention and security requirements; no retailer secrets in the extension. No hosted service or AWS deployment is required for the current demo.

title: [CS-18] Provider-backed BNPL comparison
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want current provider-backed payment terms so I can compare full obligations.

Entry criteria: current terms and integration permission obtained; jurisdiction/disclosure requirements reviewed; no estimated APR or invented financing offer. The Alpha calculator accepts user-entered terms only.

title: [CS-19] Accessibility and browser support expansion
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want verified keyboard, screen-reader and browser support for the shopping flows.

Entry criteria: actual accessibility findings, defined target browser versions, and acceptance testing on those targets. Automated DOM checks do not prove screen-reader behavior or Chrome side-panel compatibility.

title: [CS-20] Chrome Web Store beta distribution
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want a Chrome Web Store beta so installation and updates are easier.

Entry criteria: Alpha blockers addressed, privacy policy and listing assets ready, permissions justified, and current store review requirements satisfied. The current Alpha is a ZIP installed locally through Load unpacked.

title: [REL-01] Smoke-test the release ZIP in real Chrome
label: release
body: Automated Alpha 0.1.1 smoke passed October 11, 2026: https://github.com/qarteu/cartscope/actions/runs/38178299418. The actual release ZIP was unpacked and loaded in disposable Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34 on Ubuntu. All 16 browser checks passed, including toolbar activeTab access, HTTP fixture capture/category rejection, cart/compare/watch/order/financing/backup/downloads, safe input handling, responsive layouts, preview persistence, and the current 0.1.1 public demo. SHA-256: 081cb251510193a73e1d51c0caf004ee310ae6ef77d927e26e93ca92432a60d0. Actual screenshots/report: docs/visuals and docs/CHROME_TEST_RESULTS.json. Manual platform installation, native OS notification delivery, and current retailer markup remain field validation under CS-11/CS-19 and reference-user feedback.

title: [REL-02] Publish source to the personal qarteu GitHub account
label: release
body: Published and verified on October 11, 2026: public repository https://github.com/qarteu/cartscope belongs to qarteu and contains version-controlled source, MIT license, installation instructions, release tooling, automated tests, visuals, and submission documents. Publication used the authenticated qarteu account.

title: [REL-03] Publish Alpha v0.1.0 ZIP and release notes
label: release
body: Published Alpha prerelease v0.1.0 on October 11, 2026: https://github.com/qarteu/cartscope/releases/tag/v0.1.0. Tag source d015b67 contains the tested runtime, instructions, release notes, visuals, and verification records. Downloaded both release assets using gh release download; ZIP checksum matches c8918352c29aadd755dad718e4ec23f237451bcb90514a7e25b1cf53066f7283 and the hosted-tested ZIP byte-for-byte. Independently verified root manifest, version 0.1.0, 17 runtime-only files, valid CRCs, and tag README availability. Browser installation and 16 passed checks are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md and https://github.com/qarteu/cartscope/actions/runs/38174277130.

title: [REL-08] Publish and smoke-test the GitHub Pages demo
label: release
body: Published https://qarteu.github.io/cartscope/ and verified the redesigned 0.1.1 demo in fresh Chrome on October 11, 2026. https://github.com/qarteu/cartscope/actions/runs/38178299418 records HTTPS 200, current versions on landing/iframe/About, four interactive views, quantity persistence across reload, and mobile document width 390/390 pixels. Static GitHub Pages, labeled samples and manual entries, no AWS setup. Evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md, docs/CHROME_TEST_RESULTS.json and desktop/mobile screenshots.

title: [REL-04] Recruit ten consenting reference testers
label: release
body: Proposed owners: Eashan (recruiting), Jake (test protocol), Kartik (release support). Confirm ten real consenting participants privately and assign R01-R10. Record participant status without public contact information. Close only after actual commitments are recorded; unassigned roster slots and recruiting profiles are not evidence of participation.

title: [REL-05] Send personalized Alpha preview invitations
label: release
body: After REL-02/03 and installation readiness, personalize docs/ALPHA_EMAIL.md and send individually to the consenting participants under REL-04 using the team's authorized email account. Record actual invited_at dates and retain delivery evidence privately. The current email is a draft and no sent announcement is claimed. Proposed owners: Eashan and Jake, with Kartik supplying release links.

title: [REL-06] Collect and triage quantitative and qualitative feedback
label: release
body: Use the Alpha feedback issue form or private email replies. Collect task completion/time and ease, clarity, usefulness and confidence ratings plus confusing/missing information and requested improvements. Distinguish installed-extension and browser-demo results; report actual denominators. Feed reproduced blockers into CS-13. Close only after real responses and a readout exist; targets are not results.

title: [REL-07] Reconcile an existing Trello board if supplied
label: release
body: No prior external Trello board URL or access was verified in the inspected CartScope files/chats. If the team supplies its existing board, verify access and reconcile stories, status and next-sprint priorities with this GitHub tracker. GitHub Issues and docs/SPRINT_BOARD.md satisfy the current assignment's similar-issue-tracker option. Keep this conditional reconciliation task pending until a real board is available; do not invent a board link.

title: [CS-22] Refine the shopping desk design and final submission
label: alpha
body: As a reviewer, I want an original, readable shopping desk and clear evidence so I can understand and demonstrate the Alpha. Implemented: warm paper/forest styling, custom focus-and-cart mark, serif desk headings, compact item records, practical copy and a responsive demo. All 65 Node tests and 16 actual Chrome checks passed for runtime 609ec4d on https://github.com/qarteu/cartscope/actions/runs/38178299418. Real screenshots, a feature/test matrix and a Canvas write-up are prepared from this evidence; release publication and downloadable final packet remain a separate REL-09 gate.

title: [REL-09] Publish Alpha 0.1.1 and the final submission packet
label: release
body: Publish a separate v0.1.1 prerelease with tested runtime ZIP/checksum and current release notes, preserving v0.1.0. Download the GitHub ZIP and compare bytes, manifest version and CRCs with hosted-tested hash 081cb251510193a73e1d51c0caf004ee310ae6ef77d927e26e93ca92432a60d0. Publish the Canvas write-up, illustrated PDF and submission bundle with genuine Chrome screenshots and exact test scope. Close only after actual release/download verification and packet publication. Ten-user invitation delivery is separately pending under REL-04/05/06.
